newsitem.title: UK: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE NAMED IN ENGLAND SQUAD DESPITE INJURY.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-GASCOIGNE NAMED IN ENGLAND SQUAD DESPITE INJURY.

text.p: England named a squad of 24, including Paul Gascoigne, for their vital World Cup group two qualifier against Italy at Wembley on February 12.
Midfielder Gascoigne is in the squad despite having his left ankle in plaster.

He picked up an injury while playing for Glasgow Rangers in a six-a-side tournament in the Netherlands but has assured manager Glenn Hoddle he will be fit to face the Italians, coming to Wembley for their first competitive match under new coach Cesare Maldini.
Tottenham's Teddy Sheringham, who scored in England's 2-0 victory over Georgia in November in their last outing, misses out after limping out of training on Monday with a nagging ankle injury.
Sheringham's Spurs team mate Darren Anderton is still a long-term casualty.

Everton's Andy Hinchcliffe is injured, former England captain David Platt, who played in Italy with Bari, Juventus and Sampdoria, has a hamstring strain and Manchester United defender Philip Neville is out with glandular fever.
Blackburn goalkeeper Tim Flowers is recalled along with team mate Graeme Le Saux. Newcastle's Robert Lee joins his team mate Alan Shearer back in the squad.
Both England and Italy go into the match with 100 percent records. England won their first three matches, Italy their first two.
Goalkeepers - David Seaman (Arsenal), Ian Walker (Tottenham Hotspur), David James (Liverpool), Tim Flowers (Blackburn).

Defenders - Gary Neville (Manchester United), Stuart Pearce (Nottingham Forest), Graeme Le Saux (Blackburn), Gareth Southgate (Aston Villa), Tony Adams (Arsenal), Sol Campbell (Tottenham Hotspur), Dominic Matteo (Liverpool)

Midfielders - Paul Ince (Inter Milan), Paul Gascoigne (Rangers), David Beckham (Manchester United), Steve McManaman (Liverpool), David Batty (Newcastle), Matthew Le Tissier (Southampton), Robert Lee (Newcastle).
Strikers - Nicky Barmby (Everton), Alan Shearer, Les Ferdinand (both Newcastle), Robbie Fowler (Liverpool), Ian Wright, Paul Merson (both Arsenal).
